public_rationale: A December 2022 technical paper explicitly describes the models' objective as predicting the next token from preceding text. That supports 'text predictors' and the autocomplete analogy on their ordinary mechanical reading. It does not establish that prediction is the only training stage, that models cannot encode factual knowledge, or that their capabilities are limited to simple sentence completion.
limitations: A training objective is not a complete account of model capabilities or deployment architecture.
Support uses the conventional-record meaning of 'database', rather than treating all encoded knowledge as a database.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are text predictors, essentially turbocharged autocomplete, not databases.

statement.excerpt: Large language models do something very different: they are not databases; they are text predictors, turbocharged versions of autocomplete.
statement.document_title: Is ChatGPT Really a “Code Red” for Google Search?

our_interpretation: Read 'autocomplete' as an analogy for predicting text continuations, not as a limit on the complexity of tasks models can perform.
Read 'not databases' in the post's stated sense of conventional systems for storing, retrieving and updating explicit records.
Assess the generative language models discussed in the late-2022 post, rather than every possible language-model architecture.
Use the November–December 2022 deployment and reporting period described by the surrounding discussion.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous technical documentation identifies text prediction as the models' underlying training or generation mechanism, rather than conventional record lookup.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Technical documentation shows that the relevant generative models principally retrieve stored records and do not predict text continuations.

evidence.explanation: The paper explicitly identifies next-token prediction as the training objective of the language models it discusses. This supports the autocomplete analogy as a mechanism description; the distinction from conventional record lookup is an inference.
